instruction: Single Storey Loading Hall IFC And Revit Structural Count Schedule CSV This task starts from scratch with no init_file inputs and no local reference images. In Revit, create a single-storey loading hall building, export the model as result.ifc, and export a Revit structural count schedule as result.csv in the Desktop. 1. The output folder contains result.ifc and result.csv; result.ifc is at least 500 bytes and result.csv is at least 20 bytes. 2. Result.ifc uses an IFC4 schema. 3. All IfcRoot GlobalId values are unique. 4. The IFC model contains exactly 1 IfcProject, 1 IfcSite, 1 IfcBuilding, 1 IfcBuildingStorey, 3 IfcSpace entities, 4 IfcWall entities, 1 IfcSlab, 1 IfcRoof, 3 IfcDoor entities, 12 IfcColumn entities, and 17 IfcBeam entities. 5. The IFC model contains 0 IfcWindow, 0 IfcStair, 0 IfcCurtainWall, and 0 IfcBuildingElementProxy entities. 6. After replacing hyphens and underscores with spaces and lowercasing names, the IfcSpace name list contains the token office at least once, service at least once, and hall at least once. 7. Result.csv is a Revit structural schedule export with exactly the headers category,count in that order and exactly 2 non-empty data rows. 8. Result.csv contains these exact category and count rows: Columns=12 and Beams=17. 9. The result.csv counts for Columns and Beams match the IFC counts of IfcColumn and IfcBeam. Any item not explicitly required may vary.
